project.name: kube-argus
project.description: Real-time Kubernetes dashboard delivered as a single Go binary with embedded React frontend, providing live cluster state, streaming pod logs, interactive web shell, JIT exec approval, YAML editing, AI-powered diagnostics, cost analysis, and OIDC authentication. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build context exclusion list that strips node_modules, build artifacts, VCS metadata, documentation, deploy manifests, and editor/IDE files from the image build to keep the build context small and avoid leaking secrets.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yaml
nodes.summary: Single-service Docker Compose definition that runs the published kube-argus image on port 8080, mounts the host kubeconfig read-only, and wires optional auth, Prometheus, and LLM gateway environment variables for local or self-hosted deployments.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ${VAR:-default} shell-style fallbacks so the compose file works out of the box even when KUBECONFIG, CLUSTER_NAME, or DEFAULT_ROLE are not set in the environment.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Three-stage Docker build that compiles the React frontend with Node 20, cross-compiles the Go backend statically for the target architecture without QEMU, then assembles a minimal Alpine 3.21 runtime image running as the nobody user on port 8080.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses BUILDPLATFORM/TARGETARCH split so Go cross-compiles natively on the build host (CGO_ENABLED=0, -ldflags='-s -w') instead of emulating the target via QEMU, dramatically speeding up multi-arch builds.

nodes.name: ci.yaml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs on pull requests and pushes to master/main, performing parallel Go backend build/vet and TypeScript frontend build with npm caching.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses concurrency group with cancel-in-progress to supersede outdated runs for the same ref.

nodes.name: pages-sync.yaml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that syncs the docs/ landing page (index.html and screenshots) to the gh-pages branch whenever docs/ changes on master/main.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses path filters on push trigger and a dual checkout pattern (source + gh-pages target) to copy files between branches.

nodes.name: release.yaml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions release pipeline triggered on v* tags that builds and pushes multi-arch (amd64/arm64) Docker images to GHCR, packages and publishes the Helm chart to both an OCI registry and the gh-pages Helm repo, and creates a GitHub Release with CHANGELOG-derived notes.
nodes.languageNotes: Coordinates four jobs (docker, helm, helm-pages, github-release) with needs dependencies; uses docker/build-push-action with QEMU+Buildx for multi-platform builds and GHCR cache backend.

nodes.name: values.schema.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema (draft-07) validating values.yaml structure with typed property definitions for image, service, ingress, env, resources, RBAC, JIT, and scheduling settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Helm uses values.schema.json to validate user-supplied values at install/upgrade time, failing fast on invalid types or missing required fields.

nodes.name: values.yaml
nodes.summary: Default Helm values for kube-argus covering replica count, image, service/ingress, env vars, RBAC, security contexts, JIT settings, and topology constraints.

nodes.name: clusterrole.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template that provisions the cluster-wide RBAC permissions for kube-argus, defining a ClusterRole with read/write access to core, apps, batch, networking, autoscaling, policy, storage, and metrics APIs plus a ClusterRoleBinding to the chart's ServiceAccount.
nodes.languageNotes: Gated by .Values.rbac.create; grants broad cluster read plus targeted write/patch verbs (node patching, pod exec/delete, scale subresources, eviction) required by kube-argus's dashboard and JIT features.

nodes.name: deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template rendering the primary kube-argus Deployment with container image, port 8080, health probes (startup/liveness/readiness on /health), resource limits, JIT-related env vars, and optional envFrom secret reference.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses include helpers (kube-argus.fullname, kube-argus.labels, kube-argus.selectorLabels) and conditional blocks for podAnnotations, securityContext, nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity, topologySpreadConstraints, and JIT persistence env injection.

nodes.name: ingress.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template that conditionally renders a networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress exposing the kube-argus service, with configurable ingressClassName, TLS hosts/secrets, annotations, and per-host path rules pointing at the http port.
nodes.languageNotes: Gated by .Values.ingress.enabled; iterates over hosts and tls collections using nested range blocks.

nodes.name: service.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template producing the kube-argus Service that fronts the Deployment pods on the configured port, forwarding to the container http target port (8080) with optional annotations.

nodes.name: serviceaccount.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template that conditionally creates the ServiceAccount bound by the ClusterRoleBinding, supporting custom annotations (e.g., IRSA / Workload Identity) via .Values.serviceAccount.annotations.
nodes.languageNotes: Gated by .Values.serviceAccount.create; the account name resolves via the kube-argus.serviceAccountName helper to allow reusing an externally managed ServiceAccount.

nodes.name: deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes Deployment and ClusterIP Service manifests that run the kube-argus container on port 8080 with liveness/readiness probes on /health, sourcing OIDC/AI credentials from the kube-argus-config Secret and injecting pod namespace plus JIT/audit ConfigMap names via env.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-document YAML file combining a Deployment and a Service into a single applyable manifest; uses envFrom secretRef with optional: true so deployment succeeds before the operator-supplied secret exists.

nodes.name: namespace.yaml
nodes.summary: Declares the kube-argus Namespace that scopes all dashboard workloads, the ServiceAccount, and the config Secret.

nodes.name: rbac.yaml
nodes.summary: Defines the kube-argus ServiceAccount plus a ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding granting the dashboard cluster-wide read access (and selective write/exec/eviction rights) over core, apps, batch, networking, autoscaling, policy, storage, and metrics resources.
nodes.languageNotes: Permissions are intentionally broad to support JIT actions: pod exec/delete, deployment scaling, node patch, and HPA updates — granted cluster-wide rather than namespaced.

nodes.name: secret.yaml.example
nodes.summary: Template Secret manifest documenting the kube-argus-config keys for Google SSO, generic OIDC, role/session settings, Prometheus access, optional LLM gateway, and AWS region; users copy to secret.yaml and fill in values before applying.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses stringData (not data) so values are plain text rather than base64-encoded; commented blocks indicate optional auth providers.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Vite HTML entry point for the kube-argus web UI; sets dark theme defaults, declares the root mount node, and loads the React entry module src/main.tsx.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses native ES module script tag to load the TypeScript React entry, relying on Vite's dev/build pipeline for transformation.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Frontend package manifest declaring the React 19 + Vite + Tailwind stack along with xterm, recharts, and js-yaml dependencies; defines dev, build, lint, and preview scripts for the web workspace.
nodes.languageNotes: ESM package ("type": "module") requiring Node >= 20; build runs project-references TypeScript build before Vite bundles.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Root TypeScript configuration that delegates to two project references — tsconfig.app.json for the React app sources and tsconfig.node.json for the Vite tooling config.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TypeScript project references with empty files array, enabling incremental builds across the app and node-side configs.

nodes.name: tsconfig.app.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript configuration for the React application sources under web/src; enables strict mode, bundler module resolution, react-jsx, and Vite client types.
nodes.languageNotes: Sets noEmit true with verbatimModuleSyntax and erasableSyntaxOnly — typical Vite-bundled app where tsc only type-checks.

nodes.name: tsconfig.node.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript configuration scoped to the Node-side Vite config file (vite.config.ts); enables strict checks with Node types and ES2023 target.
nodes.languageNotes: Narrow include of only vite.config.ts isolates Node typings from the browser app, avoiding type pollution.

nodes.name: config.go
nodes.summary: ConfigMap and Secret listing, content inspection, and config-drift detection comparing live values against the versions referenced by running pods.

nodes.name: apiConfigDrift
nodes.summary: HTTP handler reporting ConfigMaps and Secrets whose ResourceVersion has changed since pods last mounted them.

nodes.name: computeConfigDrift
nodes.summary: Compares pod-mounted ConfigMap/Secret references against current ResourceVersions to detect stale mounts that require a pod restart.

nodes.name: apiConfigs
nodes.summary: Lists ConfigMaps and Secrets across namespaces with metadata, owner references, and pod-mount counts.

nodes.name: apiConfigData
nodes.summary: Returns the decoded data keys of a specific ConfigMap or Secret, redacting Secret values unless the caller is an admin.

nodes.name: exec.go
nodes.summary: WebSocket-based exec proxy that streams a shell session inside a target pod container by adapting the WebSocket frame I/O to client-go's remotecommand executor.

nodes.name: wsTerminal
nodes.summary: Adapter implementing io.Reader and io.Writer over a WebSocket connection so client-go's remotecommand stream can speak to the browser terminal.

nodes.name: apiExec
nodes.summary: WebSocket handler that authorizes the request, opens a remotecommand exec stream against the target pod/container, and pipes the WS connection to it.

nodes.name: helpers.go
nodes.summary: Miscellaneous formatting helpers for namespaces, durations, pod status display, and image short names used across the API handlers.

nodes.name: apiNamespaces
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning the sorted list of namespace names visible to the dashboard.

nodes.name: podDisplayStatus
nodes.summary: Derives the human-friendly pod status string used by the dashboard, combining phase, container waiting reasons, and termination signals.

nodes.name: jit.go
nodes.summary: Just-In-Time access workflow allowing users to request temporary elevated permissions on a specific workload, with admin approval, expiry, persistence, and Slack/webhook notification hooks.

nodes.name: jitRequest
nodes.summary: Struct representing a JIT access request with requester, target resource, requested duration, status, and approval metadata.

nodes.name: jitApprove
nodes.summary: Marks a JIT request as approved, records the approver and timestamps, and triggers downstream notifications.

nodes.name: jitDeny
nodes.summary: Marks a JIT request as denied and records the denier, timestamps, and notification fan-out.

nodes.name: jitInitPersistence
nodes.summary: Initializes the JIT persistence layer by restoring from disk and starting periodic save plus expiry loops.

nodes.name: jitPersist
nodes.summary: Atomically persists active and historical JIT requests to disk using a temp-file rename pattern.

nodes.name: hasActiveJIT
nodes.summary: Checks whether the given user currently holds an approved, non-expired JIT grant for a specific workload owner.

nodes.name: requireAdminOrJIT
nodes.summary: Authorization guard that allows the request when the caller is admin or holds an active JIT grant for the target resource.

nodes.name: resolvePodOwner
nodes.summary: Walks owner references from a pod up to its controlling workload kind/name so JIT grants can be scoped to the workload.

nodes.name: jitExpiryLoop
nodes.summary: Background goroutine that periodically scans active JIT grants and transitions expired ones to the expired state.

nodes.name: apiJITRequests
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning the list of pending JIT requests awaiting admin action.

nodes.name: apiJITCreate
nodes.summary: HTTP handler that creates a new JIT request from the authenticated user with validation and admin notification.

nodes.name: apiJITList
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning the full JIT request history with optional filters by status and requester.

nodes.name: apiJITMyGrants
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning the active JIT grants currently held by the requesting user.

nodes.name: apiJITAction
nodes.summary: HTTP handler routing approve/deny/cancel actions on a specific JIT request, enforcing admin role and notification fan-out.

nodes.name: main.go
nodes.summary: Application entry point that initializes logging, Kubernetes client, cache loops, auth/Prometheus/Slack/webhook subsystems, then registers all HTTP/WebSocket routes and starts the server.
nodes.languageNotes: Embeds the React web/dist via Go's embed.FS so the production binary serves both the SPA and the JSON API from a single process.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Program entry point that wires up logging, Kubernetes clients, caches, auth, integrations, HTTP route registration, and graceful shutdown.

nodes.name: initLogger
nodes.summary: Initializes the structured slog logger with the configured level and JSON or text handler.

nodes.name: kubeConfig
nodes.summary: Resolves the Kubernetes REST config from in-cluster service account, KUBECONFIG env var, or default kubeconfig path.

nodes.name: networking.go
nodes.summary: API handlers for Kubernetes networking resources, listing and describing Ingresses and Services with detailed backend resolution, ports, and policy summaries.

nodes.name: apiIngresses
nodes.summary: HTTP handler listing Ingresses across namespaces with hosts, paths, TLS settings, and class metadata.

nodes.name: apiIngressDescribe
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning a detailed Ingress description including backend Service resolution, port mappings, and TLS secret references.

nodes.name: apiServices
nodes.summary: HTTP handler listing Services across namespaces with type, ports, selectors, and endpoint counts.

nodes.name: apiServiceDetail
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning detailed Service info including endpoint slices, target pods, and load balancer status.

nodes.name: nodes.go
nodes.summary: Node listing and lifecycle action handler covering cordon, drain, uncordon, label edits, taint edits, and reboot/terminate orchestration with audit logging.

nodes.name: apiNodes
nodes.summary: HTTP handler listing nodes with capacity, allocatable, conditions, taints, pod counts, and metrics-server samples.

nodes.name: apiNodeAction
nodes.summary: Large multi-action HTTP handler dispatching node operations (cordon, uncordon, drain, label/taint edit, reboot, terminate) with role enforcement and audit recording.

nodes.name: overview.go
nodes.summary: Dashboard overview handler aggregating cluster-wide health, capacity, workload status, and event highlights into a single JSON payload.

nodes.name: apiOverview
nodes.summary: Builds the cluster overview payload by aggregating node, pod, workload, event, and capacity statistics from the cache.

nodes.name: pods.go
nodes.summary: Pod listing, detail, and restart-timeline handlers backed by both Prometheus kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and a fallback that scans events when Prometheus is unavailable.

nodes.name: restartEvent
nodes.summary: Struct describing a single container restart event used to compose the restart timeline UI.

nodes.name: restartTimelineResponse
nodes.summary: Response envelope returning the source (Prometheus or fallback) plus the ordered list of restart events for a pod.

nodes.name: apiPods
nodes.summary: HTTP handler listing pods across namespaces with display status, resource usage, owner references, and node placement.

nodes.name: apiPodDetail
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning detailed pod info including containers, init containers, volumes, conditions, events, and recent logs.

nodes.name: apiRestartTimeline
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning the chronological restart timeline for a pod, preferring Prometheus data with an events-based fallback.

nodes.name: restartTimelineFromProm
nodes.summary: Builds the pod restart timeline by querying Prometheus restart counter deltas across the requested time range.

nodes.name: restartTimelineFromFallback
nodes.summary: Fallback restart-timeline implementation that scans Kubernetes events for BackOff/Restart patterns when Prometheus is not configured.

nodes.name: prometheus.go
nodes.summary: Prometheus HTTP query client with TTL caching, range/instant query helpers, parallel batch execution, and handlers for alerts, sizing, and per-node/pod/workload metric series.

nodes.name: promCacheEntry
nodes.summary: Cache record holding a Prometheus query response with its insertion timestamp for TTL-based expiry.

nodes.name: promMetricSeries
nodes.summary: Result wrapper pairing a Prometheus query name with its returned matrix used by the parallel query helper.

nodes.name: initPrometheus
nodes.summary: Initializes the Prometheus base URL, HTTP client, optional bearer token, and result cache from configuration.

nodes.name: promQuery
nodes.summary: Executes a Prometheus range query with TTL caching and returns the parsed matrix result.

nodes.name: promInstantQuery
nodes.summary: Executes a Prometheus instant query with caching and returns the vector result.

nodes.name: promQueryParallel
nodes.summary: Executes a set of named Prometheus queries concurrently using a worker pool and returns them keyed by name.

nodes.name: apiWorkloadSizing
nodes.summary: Computes recommended CPU/memory requests for a workload from historical Prometheus usage percentiles.

nodes.name: apiAlerts
nodes.summary: Returns active Prometheus Alertmanager alerts annotated with severity and resource scope.

nodes.name: apiMetricsNode
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning per-node CPU, memory, disk, and network time series for the dashboard charts.

nodes.name: apiMetricsPod
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning per-pod CPU and memory time series for the dashboard charts.

nodes.name: apiMetricsWorkload
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning aggregated workload-level metric series across CPU, memory, restarts, and traffic.

nodes.name: resources.go
nodes.summary: Catch-all handlers for assorted Kubernetes resources including PDBs, CronJob history and triggers, namespace cost estimates, topology spread analysis, HPA detail, events, and global search.
nodes.languageNotes: At 1435 lines this is the largest file in the package; it aggregates many small unrelated handlers that pre-date dedicated files.

nodes.name: apiPDBs
nodes.summary: HTTP handler listing PodDisruptionBudgets with selectors, allowed disruptions, and current status.

nodes.name: apiCronJobHistory
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning historical Job runs for a CronJob with status, duration, and pod logs links.

nodes.name: apiCronJobTrigger
nodes.summary: HTTP handler that manually triggers a CronJob by creating a one-off Job from its template, with admin/JIT enforcement.

nodes.name: apiNamespaceCosts
nodes.summary: Estimates hourly and monthly cost per namespace by multiplying allocated resources by per-instance on-demand pricing.

nodes.name: apiSpotInterruptions
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning AWS Spot interruption history correlated with current nodes and impacted workloads.

nodes.name: apiTopologySpread
nodes.summary: HTTP handler analyzing TopologySpreadConstraints adherence across nodes and zones for selected workloads.

nodes.name: apiEvents
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning cluster events filtered by namespace, type, and time range.

nodes.name: apiSearch
nodes.summary: Global search handler matching the query against pod, workload, node, service, ingress, and configmap names.

nodes.name: apiHPA
nodes.summary: HTTP handler listing HorizontalPodAutoscalers with current/desired replicas, target metrics, and scaling conditions.

nodes.name: apiHPADetail
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning detailed HPA info including metric history, scaling decisions, and target reference.

nodes.name: server.go
nodes.summary: HTTP server helpers including CORS middleware, gzip response writer wrapping, and JSON response shortcuts shared by all handlers.

nodes.name: gzResponseWriter
nodes.summary: ResponseWriter wrapper that transparently gzip-compresses payloads when the client accepts gzip encoding.

nodes.name: corsWrap
nodes.summary: Middleware that adds permissive CORS headers and short-circuits OPTIONS preflight requests.

nodes.name: gzipWrap
nodes.summary: Middleware that wraps the response writer with gzip compression when the client sends Accept-Encoding: gzip.

nodes.name: slack.go
nodes.summary: Slack integration for JIT request notifications with persistent config storage, interactive button callbacks, and HMAC signature verification on inbound webhooks.

nodes.name: initSlack
nodes.summary: Initializes Slack integration by restoring persisted webhook URL, channel, and signing secret from disk.

nodes.name: slackRestoreConfig
nodes.summary: Loads the Slack configuration JSON from disk into the in-memory config struct.

nodes.name: slackPersistConfig
nodes.summary: Writes the current Slack configuration to disk atomically using a temp-file rename pattern.

nodes.name: apiSlackSettings
nodes.summary: HTTP handler for GET/PUT of Slack settings (webhook URL, channel, signing secret) with admin enforcement and audit logging.

nodes.name: slackNotifyJIT
nodes.summary: Sends a Slack message announcing a new JIT request with interactive approve/deny buttons.

nodes.name: slackNotifyJITResult
nodes.summary: Sends a Slack follow-up message after a JIT request has been approved or denied.

nodes.name: slackPost
nodes.summary: Internal helper that posts a JSON payload to a Slack incoming webhook URL with logging on failure.

nodes.name: apiSlackInteract
nodes.summary: Slack interactive callback handler that verifies the signature, parses the action payload, and routes approve/deny actions into the JIT workflow.

nodes.name: verifySlackSignature
nodes.summary: Validates the X-Slack-Signature header using HMAC-SHA256 with the configured signing secret and a 5-minute timestamp tolerance.

nodes.name: sparklines.go
nodes.summary: In-memory ring buffer that captures recent pod CPU/memory samples and serves them as compact sparkline series for the dashboard.

nodes.name: sparklineBuffer
nodes.summary: Ring buffer holding the last N pod metric snapshots indexed by pod identity for sparkline rendering.

nodes.name: apiPodSparklines
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning the current pod sparkline buffer as a compact JSON payload.

nodes.name: spot_advisor.go

nodes.name: spotAdvisorData
nodes.summary: In-memory store for the parsed AWS Spot advisor dataset including interruption rates and savings percentages per instance type/region.

nodes.name: spotAdvisorEntry
nodes.summary: Single entry from the AWS Spot advisor dataset with interruption rate code and savings percentage.

nodes.name: spotInstanceTypeInfo
nodes.summary: Static metadata for an EC2 instance type including vCPU, memory, and architecture used during alternative generation.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Downloads the AWS Spot advisor dataset, parses it into the in-memory store, and updates the last-refreshed timestamp.

nodes.name: generateAlternatives
nodes.summary: Generates alternative spot-friendly instance types for a given instance, preserving CPU/memory shape and architecture.

nodes.name: generateConsolidationAlternatives
nodes.summary: Suggests larger consolidated instance types that could pack multiple smaller nodes for cost savings.

nodes.name: startSpotAdvisorLoop
nodes.summary: Starts the background goroutine that periodically refreshes the Spot advisor dataset.

nodes.name: apiSpotAdvisor
nodes.summary: HTTP handler that returns spot interruption risk scores and alternative/consolidation recommendations for cluster nodes and workloads.

nodes.name: storage.go
nodes.summary: Storage handler listing PersistentVolumes and PersistentVolumeClaims with status, capacity, StorageClass, and bound pod references.

nodes.name: apiStorage
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning PVs and PVCs with binding, capacity, StorageClass, and consumer pod metadata.

nodes.name: webhook.go
nodes.summary: Generic outbound webhook subsystem delivering JIT lifecycle events to configured endpoints with optional HMAC signing and event-type filtering.

nodes.name: webhookConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration record for a webhook endpoint including URL, signing secret, and the event types it subscribes to.

nodes.name: initWebhook
nodes.summary: Initializes webhook integration by restoring persisted configs from disk on startup.

nodes.name: webhookRestoreConfig
nodes.summary: Loads persisted webhook endpoint configurations from disk into the in-memory list.

nodes.name: webhookPersistConfig
nodes.summary: Writes the current webhook endpoint configurations to disk atomically.

nodes.name: apiWebhookSettings
nodes.summary: HTTP handler for GET/PUT of webhook endpoint configurations with admin enforcement, masking secrets in responses, and audit logging.

nodes.name: webhookNotifyJIT
nodes.summary: Fans out a JIT lifecycle event to every configured webhook endpoint that subscribes to that event type.

nodes.name: webhookPost
nodes.summary: Performs the actual HTTP POST to a webhook URL with optional HMAC-SHA256 signature header.

nodes.name: workloads.go

nodes.name: apiWorkloads
nodes.summary: HTTP handler listing all workload controllers with replicas, status conditions, owner references, and rollout progress.

nodes.name: buildContainerInfo
nodes.summary: Helper that constructs a normalized container info struct (image, resources, probes) for response payloads.

nodes.name: apiWorkloadAction
nodes.summary: Multi-action HTTP handler dispatching workload operations (scale, restart, rollback, pause, resume, edit image, delete) across Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet/Job kinds with role/JIT enforcement and audit.

nodes.name: yaml_editor.go
nodes.summary: Generic YAML view/apply endpoint that fetches a Kubernetes object as YAML and applies admin-edited updates with optional dry-run.

nodes.name: apiYaml
nodes.summary: HTTP handler that returns or applies a Kubernetes resource as YAML using the dynamic client, enforcing admin role and audit logging.

nodes.name: _helpers.tpl
nodes.summary: Helm template helper definitions providing common name, fullname, chart, and label snippets reused across the kube-argus chart manifests.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard Helm boilerplate exposing kube-argus.name, kube-argus.fullname, kube-argus.chart, and label helpers.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Ignore list controlling which files the understand-anything analyzer skips when scanning the kube-argus repository.

nodes.name: ai.go

nodes.name: initLLM
nodes.summary: Initializes the LLM client configuration from environment variables, selecting provider (Anthropic vs OpenAI), API key, and model.

nodes.name: streamLLM
nodes.summary: Issues a streaming LLM completion request and proxies the token stream to the HTTP response writer as Server-Sent Events.

nodes.name: apiAIDiagnose
nodes.summary: HTTP handler for /api/ai/diagnose that builds a pod-specific diagnostic prompt and streams an LLM-generated root cause analysis back to the caller.

nodes.name: apiAISpotAnalysis
nodes.summary: HTTP handler for /api/ai/spot-analysis that asks the LLM to evaluate AWS Spot instance risk and consolidation opportunities for the cluster.

nodes.name: buildPodDiagnosticContext
nodes.summary: Assembles a comprehensive diagnostic context for a pod by gathering events, container statuses, recent logs, owner workload, and resource pressure indicators.

nodes.name: buildSpotAdvisorContext
nodes.summary: Builds the prompt context for Spot analysis by collecting node instance types, interruption rates, and workload tolerations across the cluster.

nodes.name: auditEntry

nodes.name: presenceConn

nodes.name: onlineUser

nodes.name: wsEnvelope
nodes.summary: Envelope struct used to wrap broadcast messages sent over the presence WebSocket with a type discriminator.

nodes.name: auditRecord

nodes.name: auditInitPersistence

nodes.name: auditRestore

nodes.name: auditPersist

nodes.name: auditSync

nodes.name: broadcastToAdmins
nodes.summary: Sends a WebSocket envelope to every currently connected admin presence connection.

nodes.name: apiPresenceWS
nodes.summary: WebSocket handler that upgrades the connection and registers the caller for real-time presence and audit broadcasts.

nodes.name: apiAudit
nodes.summary: HTTP handler returning paginated audit entries filtered by actor, action, and time range.

nodes.name: getOnlineUsers
nodes.summary: Returns a snapshot of currently online dashboard users deduplicated by email for the presence feed.

nodes.name: sessionData

nodes.name: loadSecretsFromAWS

nodes.name: initAuth

nodes.name: clusterCache

nodes.name: configMeta

nodes.name: startCacheLoop

nodes.name: eslint.config.js

nodes.name: ResourceBar.tsx

nodes.languageNotes: Uses Tailwind @layer directives alongside CSS custom properties to support runtime light/dark theme switching.

nodes.name: tailwind.config.js
nodes.summary: Tailwind CSS configuration declaring content sources, the kube-argus color palette, font families, and custom keyframe animations used across the dashboard UI.

nodes.name: vite.config.ts
nodes.summary: Vite build configuration enabling the React plugin, proxying /api, /auth, and /health to the Go backend on localhost:8080 during development, and producing manual rollup chunks for React and recharts to control bundle splits.
nodes.languageNotes: Dev-server proxy keeps the embedded-frontend deployment model intact — production builds are served by the Go binary, while local dev points the SPA at a separately running backend.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Kube-Argus is: a real-time Kubernetes dashboard shipped as a single Go binary (~20 MB) with the React UI embedded inside it. The README lays out the feature set (streaming pod logs, web shell, JIT exec approval, YAML editing, AI diagnostics, cost analysis), supported clusters (full EKS, core+metrics on GKE/AKS, core on minikube/kind/k3s), and the three install paths (Docker Compose, Helm, raw manifests). Use it as a map for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: cmd/server/main.go is where the binary boots. It initializes structured logging, builds the Kubernetes client, starts the background cache loops, wires up OIDC auth, Prometheus, Slack and webhook integrations, and finally registers every HTTP and WebSocket route on the mux before calling ListenAndServe. Crucially, it also uses Go's embed.FS to bake the compiled React frontend (web/dist) into the binary so the same process serves both the JSON API and the static UI on one port.
tour.languageLesson: Go's embed.FS lets you compile static assets directly into the binary at build time using a //go:embed directive. This is what allows Kube-Argus to ship as a single self-contained executable — no separate web server, no asset directory to mount, just one file to run.

tour.title: HTTP Plumbing & Shared Helpers
tour.description: Every handler relies on the same plumbing defined in server.go: a CORS middleware that gates cross-origin requests, a gzip-wrapping ResponseWriter for compressed JSON payloads, and small writeJSON helpers so handlers don't repeat themselves. This file is small but high-leverage — almost every API route registered in main.go (Step 2) passes through these wrappers before reaching its business logic.

tour.title: Authentication & Sessions
tour.description: auth.go implements the full OIDC login flow, HMAC-signed session cookies, and admin role enforcement, plus an optional AWS Secrets Manager bootstrap path for the OIDC client secret. The frontend mirrors this on the client with AuthContext, which holds the logged-in user and exposes the bearer token used by every API call. Together they enforce that no Kubernetes data leaves the binary until the caller has a valid session.
tour.languageLesson: OIDC (OpenID Connect) sits on top of OAuth 2.0 and adds an identity layer: after the user authenticates with the provider, the app receives an ID token (a signed JWT) describing who they are. Kube-Argus exchanges that ID token for a local HMAC-signed cookie so subsequent requests don't have to re-validate the JWT on every hop.

tour.title: Kubernetes Cache Layer
tour.description: cache.go is the heart of Kube-Argus's responsiveness. Instead of hitting the API server on every UI refresh, it runs background loops that rebuild full snapshots of pods, nodes, workloads and other resources from Kubernetes informers, and periodically pulls fresh samples from metrics-server. Every handler in the next step reads from this in-process cache, which is why the dashboard can auto-refresh every 10 seconds without hammering the control plane.
tour.languageLesson: Kubernetes informers maintain a local watch-driven cache of cluster objects using client-go's SharedInformerFactory. They give you O(1) lookups without polling the API server — the kube-apiserver streams add/update/delete events over a long-lived watch connection and the informer keeps an in-memory store in sync.

tour.title: Core API Surface
tour.description: The handlers in pods.go, nodes.go, workloads.go and resources.go form the bulk of the REST surface. pods.go serves pod listings, detail views, and restart timelines (with a Prometheus-backed primary path and an events-based fallback); nodes.go and workloads.go do the same for nodes and Deployments/StatefulSets/DaemonSets; resources.go is a catch-all covering PDBs, CronJobs, HPAs, events, namespace cost, topology spread, and global search. All four read from the cache built in Step 5 so responses are sub-millisecond.

tour.title: JIT Approval Workflow
tour.description: jit.go implements one of Kube-Argus's signature features: Just-In-Time elevated access. A user submits a JIT request for a specific workload, an admin approves it, the grant expires automatically, and Slack and webhook notifications fire on every state change. The frontend counterpart, JITRequestModal.tsx, is the dialog that captures the request, polls its status, and reflects approval back to the user — together they show how a single feature spans handler, persistence, integrations, and UI.

tour.title: Frontend Application Shell
tour.description: On the browser side, main.tsx is the React entry point: it mounts <App/> wrapped in the ThemeProvider and loads the global Tailwind stylesheet. App.tsx then assembles the top-level layout (namespace picker, user menu, error boundary) and delegates to the client-side router defined in routing.ts, which maps URL paths to the feature views you'll see in Step 10. This is the mirror image of Step 2 — same single-binary, but viewed from inside the browser.

tour.title: Shared Types and Data Fetching
tour.description: Two files do disproportionate work across the frontend. types.ts (fan-in 17) defines the TypeScript shapes for every cluster resource the UI renders, keeping the API contract honest end-to-end. useFetch.tsx (fan-in 21, the most-imported file in the project) is a token-aware fetch wrapper that injects the auth cookie/header, handles JSON parsing, surfaces errors, and is reused by every view to talk to the Go backend.
tour.languageLesson: Custom React hooks are functions whose name starts with 'use' and that can call other hooks. They let you extract stateful logic (like a fetch-with-auth pattern) into a reusable unit — useFetch in this project encapsulates loading state, error handling, and token injection so individual views never deal with raw fetch() calls.

tour.title: Feature Views in Action
tour.description: The components/views directory is where the architecture pays off. NodesView and WorkloadsView render the lists you land on from the sidebar — each row backed by useFetch (Step 9) hitting the corresponding handler from Step 6. PodDetailView is the most ambitious: it has tabs for overview, logs, events, YAML, and exec, streams AI-assisted diagnoses from the LLM endpoint, renders resource bars and metrics charts, and embeds an in-browser shell over WebSocket. These three views are representative of the dozen-plus others (PodsView, ServicesView, PVCsView, ConfigView, etc.).

tour.title: Containerization & Helm Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile is a multi-stage build: a Node stage compiles the React app into web/dist, a Go stage embeds that dist (Step 2's embed.FS) into a static binary, and a final minimal stage produces an image of roughly 20 MB. For Kubernetes installs, the Helm chart in deploy/helm/kube-argus wires that image into a Deployment plus the RBAC the backend needs to read cluster state — values.yaml exposes every knob, and the templates render the manifests.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements so each stage starts from a clean image; you COPY --from=<stage> to pull artifacts from a previous stage into the next one. Kube-Argus uses this to keep the Node toolchain and the Go toolchain out of the final image, shipping only the compiled binary.

tour.title: CI/CD Release Pipeline
tour.description: The capstone is .github/workflows/release.yaml, which automates everything the previous steps describe. On a tag push it builds the frontend, compiles the Go binary for multiple architectures, builds and pushes a multi-arch container image, and publishes the Helm chart — turning a git tag into a fully deployable release without manual steps. This closes the loop from source code (Steps 2–10) to a runnable artifact (Step 11) to a published release.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use 'on' to declare triggers (e.g. tag pushes), 'jobs' to run work in parallel, and 'steps' for sequential commands inside a job. Multi-arch container images are typically built with docker buildx using QEMU emulation, producing a single manifest list that points at per-architecture image layers.
